source_question.paraphrase: When can the process of generating a result not be separated from the result by projection?

precise_target.name: Exact controlled deterministic abstraction
hypotheses: Arbitrary control type A, concrete state type X, and observation type Z.
A fixed deterministic controlled update F : A -> X -> X.
A surjective observation c : X -> Z.
For sufficiency: equal current observations imply equal next observations for the same control.
precise_target.conclusion: An exact reduced deterministic update exists if and only if observation classes respect every update; it is unique on Z and preserves trajectories under identical externally supplied control sequences.
precise_target.formal_contract: (exists Fbar, forall a x, c(F a x) = Fbar a (c x)) iff (forall a x y, c x = c y -> c(F a x) = c(F a y))
precise_target.example: Two-bit joint state (visible result, hidden rule), fixed update (x,r) -> (r,not r), observation (x,r) -> x.
precise_target.interpretation_boundary: The projection exists; its ability to support exact closed dynamics is what can fail.

obligations.statement: Exact reduced update implies observation-class compatibility.
Compatibility and surjectivity yield a reduced update.
The reduced update is unique on the observation type.
One-step preservation yields every finite controlled trajectory.
The chosen two-bit projection has equal inputs and incompatible next outputs.
The full joint-state example has exact eventual period two.

residual_gap: This is established quotient/congruence mathematics, not a new theorem.
No universal failure of process/result projection or necessity of physical time is proved.
Classical representative choice is not an executable construction for arbitrary types.
Fixed joint-state semantics does not formalize unrestricted changes of language or semantics.
No entropy, bit cost, stochastic lumpability, or hidden-state feedback-controller theorem.
Biological adequacy requires a separate model correspondence.
questions.next_bounded_step: For one chosen application, specify state, observation, action and preserved output; prove compatibility or exhibit an admissible observation collision.
questions.author_question_completion_criterion: A justified formal interpretation covering the relevant source claims beyond this one exact-next-state preservation contract.

source_question.paraphrase: How should games represent decisions that merge or split the decision makers themselves?

precise_target.name: Merge-history obstruction for membership-only splitting
hypotheses: Four persistent sites, represented by Fin 4.
A concrete state is an ordered forest of binary merge histories whose leaves contain each site exactly once.
The observation is the unordered set of unordered current member sets.
Splitting the designated first composite restores its immediate predecessor trees.
Both concrete witnesses select the same current group {0,1,2}, retain spectator {3}, and admit the split.
precise_target.conclusion: No deterministic function of current membership partition can reproduce all admissible predecessor-restoring splits; therefore no exact deterministic reduced update for the totalized controlled model exists.
precise_target.interpretation_boundary: A structural operation model with fixed leaf identities, not a complete game with changing controllers, payoffs or biological individuals.

obligations.statement: The split preserves each-site-exactly-once legality.
Both histories arise by two list-adjacent merges and all witness states are legal.
Both selected splits are admissible and retain a spectator.
Current unordered partitions are equal and next partitions differ.
Apply the checked Q04 criterion to rule out an exact reduced update.
Rule out partition-only prediction even on the admissible split domain.
Reproduce the structural collision using pinned original implementation operators.
Prove complete implementation correspondence and policy-generated reachability.
Define and analyze payoffs, controller persistence and a game solution concept.

residual_gap: Lean adjacency is forest-list adjacency; board geometry and active-agent metadata belong only to the separate execution test.
No full policy scheduler, stochastic reachability, equilibrium or payoff-preservation theorem.
Published IPDm paper-to-code version equivalence and complete program refinement are unproved.
No non-Markovness claim for every probability distribution; no entropy theorem.
Repeated splits may need recursive predecessor history; minimal sufficient memory remains a separate target.
Persistent leaf sites have no automatic interpretation as biological species, cells or cognitive selves.
questions.next_bounded_step: Specify which future operations a reduced state must predict, retain the needed history and prove sufficiency; select a payoff/controller contract before extending to a game theorem.
questions.author_question_completion_criterion: An explicit, source-adequate dynamic-player game model with justified state/controller/payoff semantics and the selected behavioral or solution-concept results.

source_question.paraphrase: How can evolutionary models be calibrated when observed histories cover very few possible outcomes?

precise_target.name: Sharp finite-sample impossible-versus-rare branch testing
hypotheses: Binary trials independently and fully observe occurrence of a designated branch.
Me produces a branch with constant known probability e, where 0 < e < 1.
Decision rules may randomize and return one of the two models.

definitions.alpha: Probability of selecting Me under M0.
definitions.beta: Probability of selecting M0 under Me.

conclusions: Minimum over randomized rules of alpha+beta equals q.
Minimum over randomized rules of max(alpha,beta) equals q/(1+q).
At n=0 these values are 1 and 1/2.
precise_target.interpretation_boundary: Finite-sample overlap under different observation laws; not structural non-identifiability from equal complete observation laws.

obligations.statement: Compute the all-zero probability q=(1-e)^n.
For any randomized rule, alpha=a and beta>=q(1-a), hence both lower bounds.
Exhibit attaining rules for the sum and minimax criteria.
Handle n=0 and rational finite examples.
Formalize the general finite-probability theorem in Lean.
Justify a biological evolutionary observation/sampling model satisfying the assumptions.

evidence.limit: Constructed randomized optima and small deterministic enumerations; not a proof by enumeration for arbitrary n and real e.

evidence.record: Coordinator conversation, bounded review of derivation, code and source page 24; no rerun or compiler invoked in that review.

residual_gap: The balanced minimax decision rule uses known e to compute q.
At fixed finite n, alternatives with arbitrarily small positive e preclude a uniform worst-error guarantee below 1/2.
For fixed e>0 errors can approach zero as n grows; no finite n gives certainty.
No general Lean probability proof for this target.
Dependent or path-dependent trials, observation error, interventions, and counterfactual extrapolation require additional models.
No complete solution of evolutionary calibration or novel statistical theorem is claimed.
questions.next_bounded_step: If formal certification is prioritized, define the finite binary sample distribution and randomized decision function, prove the shared all-zero contribution, and supply both attaining rules.
questions.author_question_completion_criterion: A source-adequate evolutionary calibration model with proved error/identifiability claims and justified links from actual data to its assumptions.
